chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: How should I proceed with the shroud? He said: “Take a cloth and bind it over his buttocks and his legs.”

I said: And the waist-wrapper? He said: “It is not counted as anything; rather, it is only made so that what is there may be held together lest anything come out of him. And that which is made from cotton is better than it. Then the shirt is torn when he has been washed, and it is removed from his feet.”
He said: “Then the shroud is a shirt without buttons and without hemming, and a turban with which his head is wrapped, and its excess is returned over his feet.”

key_terms.الْإِزَارُ: the waist-wrapper or lower wrapping associated with shrouding
key_terms.الْقَمِيصُ: the shirt used as part of the shroud
key_terms.الْقُطْنِ: cotton, mentioned here as a preferable material
key_terms.الْكَفَنِ: the burial shroud used for the deceased
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a piece of cloth used to bind and secure the body
key_terms.عِمَامَةٌ: a head-wrap or turban used in the shrouding

ai.seo_question: How should the kafan of a deceased person be prepared according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains practical rulings concerning preparing the kafan for the deceased after ghusl. It describes the use of a cloth to secure the body, clarifies the function of the waist-wrapper, and mentions features of the shirt and head-wrap used in the shrouding.
